excerpts.text:
Gender parity 

These were the most gender‑balanced Olympic Winter Games ever. Women made up 47 per cent of all athlete’s participation and competed in a record 50 women’s events. Across multiple sports, the programme moved closer to full parity – with equal distances in cross‑country skiing, increased women’s quotas in luge and bobsleigh, and additional women’s events added to the schedule. The programme also included 12 mixed events, creating further opportunities for women and men to compete together and reinforcing the Games’ ongoing push towards gender balance.

The 2026 Winter Olympics featured 116 medal events in 16 disciplines, an increase of seven events and one discipline over [Beijing 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics").

The Games had the highest percentage of women's participation in Winter Olympic history until that point ([Nordic combined](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nordic_combined_at_the_Winter_Olympics "Nordic combined at the Winter Olympics") remained the only Winter Olympic sport in which only men compete), at 47%.[[52]](#cite_note-55)[[53]](#cite_note-:3-56)[[54]](#cite_note-Inside_the_Games-57)
